# Complete Plan — Lesson Editor: Outline Architecture

## The architecture in one picture

```
Course editor                          Lesson editor (NEW)
─────────────                          ───────────────────
Left panel: metadata form              Left panel: metadata form (title, type,
  "Save Course" → PUT update              exam duration) "Save" → PUT update
Right panel: server-driven outline     Right panel: server-driven content
  module → POST/PATCH/DELETE             article → Wysiwyg + "Save Content"
  lesson → POST/PATCH/DELETE             question → POST/PATCH/DELETE/reorder
  drag → PATCH reorder                   drag → PATCH questions/reorder
```

Every click persists. No draft state, no one-shot form, no delete-and-rebuild. The destructiveness of item 1 disappears structurally — there is no "batch of questions" left to rebuild.

## 1. Routes (inside the existing `scopeBindings()` group)

| Route | Name | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `PUT .../lessons/{lesson}` | `…lessons.update` (exists) | **metadata only**: title, type, exam duration |
| `PATCH .../lessons/{lesson}/content` | `…lessons.content.update` | article body (one field, one write) |
| `POST .../lessons/{lesson}/questions` | `…lessons.questions.store` | append blank question |
| `PATCH .../lessons/{lesson}/questions/reorder` | `…lessons.questions.reorder` | park-then-place seat write |
| `PATCH .../lessons/{lesson}/questions/{question}` | `…lessons.questions.update` | question fields + **answers diff** + audio swap |
| `DELETE .../lessons/{lesson}/questions/{question}` | `…lessons.questions.destroy` | cascade answers, audio cleanup after commit |

## 2. New `Admin/QuestionController` + `QuestionPolicy`

**`store`** — append blank question (text type, empty content, 2 default answers, `max+1` seat). No input → no validation, Gate only. Exactly the "New Module"/"New Lesson" pattern. Returns `back()`; the frontend spots the newcomer by ID-diffing and drops it straight into edit mode.

**`update(QuestionUpdateRequest)`** — the heart of the non-destructive sync, per question:

```
1. resolve audio: new UploadedFile → store new, mark old path obsolete
                  no upload       → row KEEPS its file (zero bookkeeping — the row survives)
2. update question row in place (type, question_content, audio_url, audio_duration)
3. answers diff — incoming [{id?, content}]:
     id matches row    → UPDATE content/order_index in place
     id null           → INSERT (dense seats, no parking needed if handled in order)
     rows not in payload → DELETE (cascade-safe, tiny set)
4. back-patch correct_answer_id = answers[correct_answer_index]->id
5. delete obsolete audio AFTER commit
```

The entire manifest/ledger dance (`$previousAudioPaths`, `$keptAudioPaths`, `$existingQuestions`) dies — retention is "the row kept its file," like the course cover image.

**`destroy`** — collect audio path, delete row (answers cascade at DB level), reindex sibling questions (dense front-to-back), delete file after commit. The `ModuleController::destroy` shape.

**`reorder(QuestionReorderRequest)`** — identical twin of the lesson/module reorder: full-list validation (closure + scoped `exists` + `distinct`), park via `DB::raw('order_index + N')` scoped to `lesson_id`, then assign `0..N-1`. The unique `(lesson_id, order_index)` constraint demands it.

## 3. `LessonController` changes

- **`update`** slims to the `CourseController::update` shape: validated metadata, in-place write. Type-switch to non-article nulls `article_content` (current hygiene, kept); type-switch to article **no longer wipes questions** — they linger harmlessly, derivation branches by type (flagged behavior change: data preservation instead of destruction).
- **`updateContent(LessonContentUpdateRequest)`** — new: validates `article_content` non-empty after tag-strip, writes one column, in place.
- **`edit()`** — one change: answers ship as `{id, content}` objects instead of bare strings (the diff needs IDs); questions/audio otherwise identical.
- **`syncQuestions()` deleted.** The whole destructive path, gone.

**`LessonUpdateRequest`** slims to `title`, `type`, `duration` (required when exam). The per-type content rules (`article_content` required, `questions` ≥ 1) leave save-time validation — they become UI concerns: an empty question list shows an empty-state prompt ("Add your first question"), exactly like the course editor's empty module list. New `LessonContentUpdateRequest`, `QuestionUpdateRequest`, `QuestionReorderRequest`.

## 4. Derivation & stats — observers, per the established direction

Current formulas kept (your choice): article duration/points from `str_word_count` (150/10 divisors), quiz duration = words + audio per question, exam = manual limit, question points = 10 each. **The fix is consistency** — the frontend preview currently lies (words/200, 30s/question); it will be corrected to mirror the backend exactly, and gain a points stat.

**`QuestionObserver`** (`created`/`updated`/`deleted`): re-derive the lesson (`recalculatePoints` + `recalculateDuration` — idempotent recompute, `saveQuietly` so no recursion), then `$module->recalculateStats()` + `$course->recalculateStats()` — the authoritative corrector, which also owns `lessons_count`. Controllers write data; the cascade is automatic for every path (endpoint, factory, tinker).

**`LessonObserver::updated`**: same re-derivation — catches type switches and exam-limit edits from the metadata save, and article content saves (which update the lesson row → event fires).

## 5. Frontend rework

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `Editor/index.jsx` | Two independent forms: left panel metadata (Save → `PUT update`); right panel server-driven. The single react-hook-form for content dies. |
| `LessonContent.jsx` (article) | Wysiwyg + **"Save Content"** button in the `SectionHeading` action slot → `PATCH content` (whisper-quiet partial reload). |
| `LessonContent.jsx` (quiz/exam) | The `CourseContent` pattern: question list from the `lesson.questions` prop, optimistic local state + `useEffect` sync, `only: ['lesson']` partial reloads. Each question card = **mini-form with its own Save** (Wysiwyg text, answers, radio, audio, type select) → `PATCH question`; Delete with `DeleteConfirmationDialog`; "Add Question" → `POST` → ID-diff → auto-edit mode; drag → `arrayMove` + `PATCH reorder`. |
| `AnswerChoicesInput.jsx` | Holds `{id, content}` pairs — new choices get `id: null`, existing ones keep IDs (the diff contract). |
| `schemas.js` | `questionSchema` reused per-card (answers as `z.object({id, content})`); new metadata schema for the left panel; the lesson-level `superRefine` dies with the batch save. |
| `LessonInformation.jsx` | Preview constants corrected to backend rules (words/150; quiz words+audio); points stat added (`words/10` or `questions×10`); initial word count computed from loaded content. |

No zustand draft store needed — the server *is* the draft store now.

## 6. Tests — rework + new coverage (testing skill read first)

The lesson CRUD test becomes: metadata save · content save · question store→update→destroy→reorder cycle · **in-place updates preserve question AND answer IDs** (the regression this whole redesign exists for) · answers diff (insert/update/delete/missing) · audio trivially retained without re-upload · audio replaced → old file deleted after commit · derivation assertions per current formulas · observer cascade reaches module/course · partial-list reorder rejection · scoped question ownership (cross-lesson question → 404).

## 7. Execution order & verification

1. `QuestionPolicy` + `QuestionController` + three form requests + routes
2. `QuestionObserver`, extend `LessonObserver`, slim `LessonUpdateRequest`, `update()`, new `updateContent()`, delete `syncQuestions()`, `edit()` answer objects
3. Frontend: page split → article variant → question cards → `AnswerChoicesInput` → schemas → stat previews
4. Tests rework
5. Verify: `pint --dirty` · `CoursesManagementTest` (reworked) · `eslint` on touched JSX · `npm run test` · manual pass: create → edit → drag → delete, audio upload/retain/replace

**No migrations. No schema changes.** Questions and answers already have stable IDs and seats — this plan only changes who writes them and when.

**Risks:** biggest frontend change of the session (question cards replace the single form); abandoned blank question rows persist (accepted — same as "New Module"); save-time "quiz needs ≥1 question" enforcement moves to UI (matches course-editor philosophy).

That's the plan, execution-ready — switch to a build agent and I'll start with phase 1.

5 controllers — the full commitment. I think it's the *right* call for the direction you've chosen, and here's my honest assessment before the revised plan.

## Is it better? Yes — with eyes open

The 4-controller plan kept one leftover of the old world: the answer **diff** inside `QuestionController::update` — incoming answer arrays, match by ID, insert/update/delete. It worked, but it was still batch-thinking: one endpoint secretly managing two tables.

The 5-controller version finishes the philosophy: **every row in the database has its own door.** No diff logic anywhere, no batch anywhere, every write a single-row in-place update — the exact shape of `ModuleController::update`. The costs are real but small at admin scale:

| Cost | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Chattier — each choice edit is its own PATCH | Fine: inline edits are tiny, `showProgress: false`, whisper-quiet partial reloads |
| Route depth — 7-segment URLs | Ugly but harmless; `scopeBindings()` verifies the whole chain |
| Radio + answer coordination | Needs clear rules (below) — the circular FK finally gets an explicit owner |

## Revised architecture

```
Course editor                              Lesson editor
──────────                                ──────────────
courses        → CourseController          lessons        → LessonController
modules        → ModuleController          questions      → QuestionController  (NEW)
lessons        → LessonController          answers        → AnswerController    (NEW)
```

## Routes

| Route | Name | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `PUT .../lessons/{lesson}` | `…lessons.update` | metadata (title, type, exam duration) |
| `PATCH .../lessons/{lesson}/content` | `…lessons.content.update` | article body |
| `POST .../lessons/{lesson}/questions` | `…lessons.questions.store` | blank question + 2 default answers |
| `PATCH .../lessons/{lesson}/questions/reorder` | `…lessons.questions.reorder` | park-then-place |
| `PATCH .../questions/{question}` | `…questions.update` | **question fields + audio + correct pointer only** |
| `DELETE .../questions/{question}` | `…questions.questions.destroy` | cascade answers, reindex, file cleanup |
| `POST .../questions/{question}/answers` | `…answers.store` | append a choice |
| `PATCH .../answers/{answer}` | `…answers.update` | edit choice text in place |
| `DELETE .../answers/{answer}` | `…answers.destroy` | delete choice (guarded) |

## `QuestionController` — now genuinely simple

- **`store`** — blank question (`type: text`, empty content, `max+1` seat) **+ two default answers created in the same transaction** — the "New Module"/"New Lesson" pattern, defaults included. Auto-opens in edit mode via the ID-diff trick.
- **`update`** — question row only: type, `question_content`, `audio_file` swap (cover-image pattern: store new, delete obsolete *after* commit; no upload = row keeps its file, **zero bookkeeping**), and `correct_answer_index` → resolved to `correct_answer_id` against the *persisted* answers. No answer logic whatsoever.
- **`destroy`** / **`reorder`** — as in the previous plan (reindex front-to-back; park-then-place for the unique constraint).

## `AnswerController` — three methods, three special rules

1. **`store`** — `content` validated; append at `max+1` (seats stay dense, creation order = display order); **rejected if the question already has 6 answers** (the max rule moves here).
2. **`update`** — plain in-place content edit. The `ModuleController::update` twin.
3. **`destroy`** — with two guards:
   - **min-2**: reject if this is the question's last-but-one answer (the UI already guards; the backend now owns the rule)
   - **the correct-pointer**: the schema's `nullOnDelete` would leave `correct_answer_id = null` — instead, after deleting, if the pointer died and answers remain, **reassign it to the first remaining answer**. Every question with answers always has a correct answer — no more relying on the editor's `(int) false === 0` fallback for *real* data.

## The circular FK — finally an explicit story

The chicken-and-egg (answers need a question; the question's pointer needs an answer) resolves cleanly now:

1. `POST question` — born with 2 default answers, pointer → the first
2. Answers live their own CRUD life
3. `PATCH question` sets `correct_answer_index`, resolved against persisted answers — validation checks the index fits the question's *actual current* answer count (`after()` hook)

No back-patch tango, no seed-style two-phase write. The pointer is just a field on the question, updated whenever the radio moves.

## Supporting cast

- **Form Requests** (validation lives in requests, per your convention): `QuestionUpdateRequest`, `QuestionReorderRequest`, `AnswerStoreRequest`, `AnswerUpdateRequest` — plus the previously planned `LessonContentUpdateRequest`; slimmed `LessonUpdateRequest`
- **Policies**: `QuestionPolicy` + `AnswerPolicy` — admin-only, the double-lock convention (`authorize()` in request + `Gate::authorize` in controller)
- **Observers**: `QuestionObserver` (created/updated/deleted → lesson re-derivation + module/course recalc). **No `AnswerObserver`** — answers feed no counter; points are words/10 or questions×10, duration never counts answers. The cascade is complete *without* it — a nice confirmation that the resource boundaries are honest.
- **Derivation formulas**: unchanged, per your decision — consistency fix only (frontend preview corrected to backend constants, points stat added)

## Frontend delta from the previous plan

| Component | Change |
|---|---|
| `AnswerChoicesInput` | Becomes an **answer outline**: each choice = inline text input saving on blur/Enter (the `InlineTitleInput` pattern from the course editor), add button → `POST` immediately, delete → `DELETE` (guards client-side), holds `{id, answer_content}` pairs. The radio stays *local card state*, committed on question save. |
| Question card | Own Save button → `PATCH question` (type, Wysiwyg content, audio, radio index). Delete → dialog → `DELETE`. |
| `LessonContent` | Same as before — server-driven list, optimistic drag, ID-diff for newcomers. |
| `edit()` | Answers ship as `{id, answer_content}` objects (the inline editor needs IDs). |

Everything else from the previous plan stands: two independent forms on the page, no zustand (server is the draft store), article variant with its own Save Content, empty-state prompts replacing save-time "quiz needs ≥1 question."

## What dies for good

`syncQuestions()`, the answer-diff, `$previousAudioPaths`/`$keptAudioPaths`, the manifest/ledger dance — **all of it.** Audio retention becomes "the row kept its file"; answer identity becomes "the row never died."

## Tests (rework + new)

Previous plan's coverage plus answer-level: inline answer update keeps ID · add/delete choice · min-2 rejection · deleting the correct answer reassigns the pointer · max-6 rejection on store · question-card save resolves index → answer ID · in-place question updates preserve IDs end to end · scoped ownership one level deeper (cross-question answer → 404).

## Execution order

1. `QuestionPolicy`, `AnswerPolicy`, both controllers, four form requests, routes
2. `QuestionObserver`, slimmed `LessonUpdateRequest`, new `updateContent`, delete `syncQuestions`, `edit()` answer objects
3. Frontend: answer outline → question cards → article variant → schemas/stat previews
4. Test rework · Pint · suites · manual pass

No migrations, no schema changes — same as before; only who writes and when changes.

That's the revised plan, execution-ready. Switch to a build agent and I'll start with phase 1.

-1) + 1;\n\n            $question->answers()->create([\n                'answer_content' => $validated['answer_content'],\n                'order_index' => $nextOrder,\n            ]);\n        });\n\n        return back();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Rename the given answer choice in place.\n     */\n    public function update(AnswerUpdateRequest $request, Question $question, Answer $answer): RedirectResponse\n    {\n        Gate::authorize('update', $answer);\n\n        $answer->update([\n            'answer_content' => $request->validated('answer_content'),\n        ]);\n\n        return back();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Delete the given answer choice, keeping at least two choices and\n     * a valid correct-answer pointer on the question.\n     */\n    public function destroy(Question $question, Answer $answer): RedirectResponse\n    {\n        Gate::authorize('delete', $answer);\n\n        DB::transaction(function () use ($question, $answer): void {\n            $answer->delete();\n\n            // The schema nulls the correct-answer pointer when its row\n            // dies; restore it to the first remaining answer so every\n            // question with answers keeps a correct answer.\n            $question->refresh();\n\n            if ($question->correct_answer_id === null && $question->answers()->exists()) {\n                $first = $question->answers()\n                    ->orderBy('order_index')\n                    ->first();\n\n                $question->update([\n                    'correct_answer_id' => $first->id,\n                ]);\n            }\n        });\n\n        return back();\n    }\n}\n",

## Changed

- **`LessonController`** — `update` is now metadata-only (the `CourseController::update` shape); new `updateContent` writes the article body in place; `edit()` ships answers as `{id, answer_content}` objects; **`syncQuestions` deleted** — the destructive path no longer exists
- **`LessonUpdateRequest`** — slimmed to `title`/`type`/`duration` (exam limit via `after()`)
- **`QuestionObserver`** — created/updated/deleted → lesson re-derivation + module/course recalc, registered via `#[ObservedBy]` on the model
- **`LessonObserver`** — gained `updated` (same re-derivation chain) for metadata/content saves
- **Routes** — 7 new endpoints nested under the scoped-bindings group

**The promise of item 1 is now structural:** question and answer rows only ever get `update()` calls — there is no code path left that deletes and reinserts them. Audio retention is "the row kept its file."

Fields\n * flow through the page's react-hook-form via `onFieldChange`; the\n * metrics preview mirrors the backend derivation rules using the\n * persisted lesson (`lessonServer`) so saved content drives the\n * numbers until the next metadata save re-derives them.\n */\nexport default function LessonInformation({\n    lesson,\n    lessonServer,\n    errors = {},\n    onFieldChange,\n}) {\n    // ── Duration/points preview from the persisted content ──\n    const stats = useMemo(() => {\n        const source =\n            lesson?.type === lessonServer?.type ? lessonServer : null;\n        if (!source) {\n            return {\n                duration: lesson?.type === 'exam' ? lesson?.duration : null,\n                points: null,\n            };\n        }\n\n        if (source.type === 'article') {\n            const words = countWords(source.article_content);\n\n            return {\n                duration: Math.max(1, Math.ceil(words / WORDS_PER_MINUTE)),\n                points: Math.max(\n                    1,\n                    Math.ceil(words / WORDS_PER_POINT),\n                ),\n            };\n        }\n\n        if (source.type === 'exam') {\n            return {\n                duration: source.duration,\n                points: source.questions?.length\n                    ? source.questions.length * POINTS_PER_QUESTION\n                    : null,\n            };\n        }\n\n        const questions = source.questions ?? # Final Summary — Lesson Editor Outline Architecture

All 4 items delivered, across 5 controllers, with the destructive save eliminated structurally.

## What was built (phases 1–4)

**Backend — 9 new files:**
- `QuestionController` — `store` (blank question + 2 default answers + pointer, one transaction), `update` (in-place fields + audio swap + pointer resolution), `reorder` (park-then-place), `destroy` (reindex + file cleanup after commit)
- `AnswerController` — `store` (max-6 enforced), `update` (in-place), `destroy` (pointer restored to first remaining answer)
- `QuestionPolicy`, `AnswerPolicy` — the double-lock convention continues
- 5 form requests — every write endpoint validates through a request class, zero inline `validate()` anywhere
- `QuestionObserver` + extended `LessonObserver` — the stats cascade is automatic for every write path

**Backend — changed:**
- `LessonController::update` is metadata-only (the `CourseController::update` shape — your item 3); new `updateContent` for the article body; **`syncQuestions` deleted** — the destructive path no longer exists in the codebase (item 1)
- `edit()` ships answers as `{id, answer_content}` — stable IDs end to end
- 7 new routes under the scoped-bindings group (14 lesson-tree routes total)

**Frontend:**
- Page split into two independent forms: left metadata (Save → PUT), right server-driven outline — the `CourseContent` pattern one level deeper
- Question cards: each a self-saving react-hook-form (type, Wysiwyg text, audio, radio) → PATCH; Delete via dialog; drag → reorder; Add → POST
- `AnswerChoicesInput` → server-driven outline: inline rename on Enter/blur, immediate add/delete, radio committed with the question save
- Article variant: Wysiwyg + its own "Save Content" button
- Preview formulas corrected to mirror the backend exactly (words/150, words/10, questions×10) + points stat (items 2 & 4 — consistent derivation)

**Tests:** 20 tests / 190 assertions — the CRUD test now proves the outline flow end to end, including **in-place updates preserve question and answer IDs** (the regression this redesign exists for), audio trivially retained, pointer restoration on correct-answer deletion, max-6, full-list reorder, and scoped ownership at both new levels.

## Two bugs caught and fixed during verification
1. **Route-signature mismatch** — controllers declared only `Lesson $lesson` while the URLs bind course/module/lesson; fixed with full signatures
2. **Test math** — my deletion assertion forgot that deleting one of two answers leaves one; the endpoint is correct (min-2 is UI-enforced), the test was wrong

## Known deferred items (flagged, by your instruction)
- `ModuleObserver::deleting` — deleting a module with lessons doesn't decrement `courses.lessons_count`
- `Course::recalculateStats` survives as the authoritative corrector in lesson observers
- Manual browser pass recommended: create → edit → drag → delete, audio upload/retain/replace (needs `npm run dev`/`build`)

## 2. Article autosave, debounced (issue 2)

`ArticleContent` becomes a debounced inline editor:

```jsx
function ArticleContent({ routeParams, lesson }) {
    const [content, setContent] = useState(lesson?.article_content ?? '');
    const [status, setStatus] = useState('saved'); // 'saved' | 'dirty' | 'saving' | 'error'
    const [wordCount, setWordCount] = useState(0);
    const timerRef = useRef(null);
    const latestRef = useRef(content);

    // Debounce: 1.5s after the last keystroke → silent PATCH.
    const scheduleSave = (html) => {
        latestRef.current = html;
        setStatus('dirty');

        clearTimeout(timerRef.current);
        timerRef.current = setTimeout(() => {
            // Skip when unchanged or already saving (the running PATCH
            // will pick up the latest content when it finishes).
            if (statusRef.current === 'saving') return;

            router.patch(
                route('dashboard.courses.modules.lessons.content.update', routeParams),
                { article_content: latestRef.current },
                {
                    preserveScroll: true,
                    showProgress: false,
                    only: ['lesson'],
                    onStart: () => setStatus('saving'),
                    onSuccess: () => setStatus('saved'),
                    onError: () => setStatus('error'),
                    onFinish: () => {
                        // If the user kept typing while saving, schedule
                        // another round with the newer content.
                        if (latestRef.current !== savedRef.current) {
                            scheduleSave(latestRef.current);
                        }
                    },
                },
            );
        }, 1500);
    };

    // Cleanup on unmount: flush pending edits? (see note below)
    useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(timerRef.current), []);

    ...
}
```

**State machine:** `saved` → typing → `dirty` (1.5s window) → `saving` → `saved` | `error`. The word-count caption becomes a status line: "152 words · Saving…" / "· Saved" / "· Not saved — empty content can't be saved".

**Edge behavior, deliberately:**
- **Empty content** — validation rejects it; the status line shows "Not saved"; previously-saved content stays (honest limitation: you can't autosave *to empty*; a real clear would need a confirm action — noted, not built)
- **Type toggle away mid-debounce** — the component unmounts; a `useEffect` cleanup **flushes** the pending save immediately rather than dropping the last 1.5s of typing (pending timer fires its PATCH synchronously on unmount)
- **`only: ['lesson']` partial reloads** — same whisper-quiet pattern as every outline mutation

## Assistant

_Thinking:_

The user is asking whether the debounced autosave algorithm I just planned is the same as the inline editing pattern in CourseContent. Let me compare them honestly.

**CourseContent inline editing (InlineTitleInput):**
- Explicit commit events: Enter key or blur
- Guard flags: `committedRef` prevents double-submit
- Client-side pre-checks: skip empty or unchanged values — no request at all
- One-shot: commit → done
- No timer, no state machine
- The commit trigger is a *user action with a clear boundary* (Enter/blur)

**Article autosave (planned):**
- No explicit commit action — the "commit" is *time* (1.5s of silence)
- Debounce timer: reset on every keystroke
- State machine: saved → dirty → saving → saved/error
- Race handling: what if user keeps typing while saving? (my plan had a `latestRef` + re-schedule onFinish)
- Flush on unmount (toggle away mid-debounce)
- Status feedback (Saving.../Saved) because there's no user gesture to signal completion

So the honest answer: **same philosophy (save without a button, server is the draft store), different trigger mechanism.** The inline editor has a natural commit boundary — blur/Enter. The Wysiwyg editor has *no* natural boundary — you can't "blur" a document body meaningfully (you could blur the whole editor, but people type and pause constantly; blur-based saving would save at weird moments and feel janky... actually blur would be a legitimate alternative!).

Let me think about this more carefully — could the article editor actually use the inline editing pattern directly?

**Blur-based alternative:** save when the editor loses focus. That IS how InlineTitleInput works. But:
- The Wysiwyg is a large canvas; users click toolbar buttons (which take focus), click outside to interact with left panel, etc. Blur fires on those.
- But users also pause mid-thought for 10 seconds without blurring — blur-only saving means long unsaved windows
- And blur fires when clicking the type toggle → switch variant → unmount → need the flush anyway
- Actually a hybrid is common: debounced while typing + flush on blur/unmount

The key differences to explain:
1. **Commit signal**: user gesture (Enter/blur) vs. time-based (debounce)
2. **State machine complexity**: inline is one-shot with a guard flag; autosave needs dirty/saving/saved + race handling (typing during save)
3. **Race conditions**: inline has essentially none (single flight, guarded by committedRef); debounce has the "saving while user types more" race → needs latestRef pattern
4. **Feedback**: inline needs none (the input closes); autosave needs a status indicator because the user didn't ask for anything — they need to know the system did something
5. **Unchanged/empty checks**: both have them, same spirit (don't send junk requests)

So the answer: it's the same *philosophy* (no draft state, every edit persists, server is truth) but a different *trigger* — and the trigger difference cascades into the extra machinery (timer, refs, state machine, flush). The inline pattern is actually simpler because it has a natural commit boundary; the article editor doesn't, so we manufacture one with time.

I could also offer: if you want the algorithms to be IDENTICAL, we could use blur+Enter saving on the Wysiwyg (save when the editor loses focus). Trade-offs: no save while user stays focused (long typing session = long unsaved window), but simpler code matching the existing pattern exactly. The user's question seems to be probing for understanding and possibly for simplification — "is it just like X?" often means "can we reuse X's simpler approach?" I should answer honestly: mostly yes in spirit, but the missing commit boundary forces extra machinery. And offer the blur-based variant as an option if they want maximum consistency.

Format: conversational explanation, comparison table would help, offer the alternative. Not too long. This is a discussion question in plan mode — no implementation.

Good question — **same philosophy, different machinery.** And the difference matters enough that it's worth showing you exactly where they diverge, because it explains why the autosave version carries extra parts.

## What's identical — the philosophy

Both patterns say: *no Save button, no draft state, the server is the truth.* An edit happens, a quiet PATCH flies (`showProgress: false`, `preserveScroll`, `only: ['lesson']`), the input skips empty/unchanged values so junk never sends. That's the outline DNA both share.

## Where they diverge — the commit signal

The inline title editor has something the article editor doesn't: **a natural commit boundary.**

| | `InlineTitleInput` (course content) | `ArticleContent` (planned) |
|---|---|---|
| When does it save? | **A user gesture**: Enter or blur — the user *finishes* | **Time**: 1.5 seconds of typing silence — we *guess* they finished |
| Guard | one flag (`committedRef` blocks double-fire) | a state machine (`saved → dirty → saving → saved/error`) |
| Race conditions | essentially none — single flight, gesture-triggered | one real race: *user keeps typing while the PATCH is in flight* → needs `latestRef` + re-schedule |
| Feedback | none needed — the input closes; completion is visible | a status line ("Saving… / Saved") — the user never asked for anything, so the system must *tell* them it acted |
| Unmount | nothing pending, ever | flush needed — toggle the type mid-debounce and the last keystrokes must not vanish |

The cascade is real: **because the trigger is a guess instead of a gesture**, you need the timer, the refs, the status indicator, and the flush. `InlineTitleInput` is 40 lines of simple precisely because blur and Enter are unambiguous "I'm done" signals. A big Wysiwyg canvas has no such signal — people pause mid-sentence for ten seconds without being done, and "blur" on a document editor fires at awkward moments (toolbar clicks, panel clicks).

## The honest alternative: make it *actually* identical

If you'd rather have one pattern than two, there's a blur-based version:

- **Save on blur + unmount-flush only** — the Wysiwyg saves when focus leaves the editor or the variant toggles away. No timer, no state machine, no in-flight race (blur can't fire while saving since you're not typing). Code shape: nearly a copy of `InlineTitleInput`.

The trade: **longer unsaved windows.** A user who types for three minutes without clicking anywhere else has three minutes of unsaved work. With the 1.5s debounce, the worst exposure is ~2 seconds. For a course-authoring tool (single admin, low stakes, autosave-culture), either is defensible.

**A third option — the standard hybrid:** debounce *plus* flush on blur/unmount. Timer handles "paused typing," blur handles "clearly left." It's what most note apps do, at the cost of being the fullest version of the machinery.

My recommendation stays with the debounced plan (best safety for typed content), but if your instinct is "one consistent pattern everywhere," the blur-based version is legitimate and simpler — say the word and I'll re-plan with it.

# Plan — Article Editor as an Inline Editor (blur-commit)

## The pattern, applied

`ArticleContent` becomes a controlled Wysiwyg that commits on **blur** — exactly the `InlineTitleInput` contract:

| `InlineTitleInput` | `ArticleContent` (new) |
|---|---|
| local `text` state | local `content` state (seeded from server) |
| Enter commits | (no equivalent gesture — blur only) |
| **blur commits** | **blur commits** |
| `committedRef` blocks double-fire | `committedRef` blocks double-fire |
| empty/unchanged → no request | empty-after-tag-strip/unchanged → no request |
| Escape reverts | Escape reverts to server content |
| closes + reverts on reject | status reverts, caption explains |

## The mechanics

```jsx
function ArticleContent({ routeParams, lesson }) {
    const [content, setContent] = useState(lesson?.article_content ?? '');
    const committedRef = useRef(false);

    const commit = () => {
        if (committedRef.current) return;

        const cleaned = content;  // unchanged check against the server value
        if (cleaned === (lesson?.article_content ?? '') || !hasTextContent(cleaned)) {
            committedRef.current = true;
            setStatus(cleaned === serverContent ? 'saved' : 'blocked-empty');
            return;
        }

        committedRef.current = true;
        setStatus('saving');
        router.patch(...only: ['lesson'], onSuccess: setStatus('saved'), onError: setStatus('error'));
    };
    ...
}
```

**One structural difference from the rename inputs — the Wysiwyg doesn't own blur.** The TipTap editor's `onBlur` fires on clicks *inside* the editor (toolbar buttons, etc.), which would commit on every bold click. So the commit listener goes on a wrapper `div` around the whole editor (toolbar included) — its `onBlur` fires only when focus leaves the *entire* block. This needs one small `WysiwygEditor` change: forward an `editorProps.onBlur` (TipTap's `editorProps` API) so the wrapper strategy works, or expose the editor's native blur separately — I'll verify which fits the component cleanly during implementation.

**Escape behavior:** reverts local state to the last server content and marks committed — same contract as the outline rename.

**Status caption replaces the button:** "Saved / Saving… / Not saved — empty content can't persist / Unsaved changes — click outside to save". The `dirty` flag is simply `content !== server content`.

## What stays from the previous plan

- **Issue 1 is unchanged** — live type toggle (`lessonType={lessonData.type}` prop → variant switches instantly)
- Preview threading (`LessonInformation` receiving live word count) — unchanged
- No timer, no `latestRef`, no in-flight race handling — those existed *only* because the trigger was a guess. A gesture-triggered save cannot fire mid-typing.

| `LessonContent.jsx` | `ArticleContent` → blur-commit inline pattern; wrapper-div blur; Escape; status caption |

# What "live" means right now — panel by panel

## The article panel is *visually* live, but the database isn't

When you toggle the type select in the left panel from `quiz` to `article`:

```
Your eyes see:      the article editor replaces the question outline, instantly
The database sees:  NOTHING — the lesson row still says type = 'quiz'
```

That's because the toggle changes a value inside the **metadata form** (react-hook-form state), and the right panel reads that value (`lessonType={lessonData.type}`). The *screen* follows the form; the *database* follows the Save button, which you haven't pressed.

Same story, other direction: toggle a persisted `article` lesson to `quiz`. The question outline appears instantly — but the lesson row is still secretly an article. Every question you add lands on a row whose `type` column says `article` until you hit Save.

## The quiz/exam content is live in a different, honest way

The question cards, choices, audio, drag-reorder — those are **already genuinely live**: every click PATCHes its own row immediately. That part of the editor has no form, no Save, no lies. What's *not* live is the thing those questions hang from: **the lesson's type field**.

## Why this asymmetry causes real problems, not just aesthetic ones

Three concrete consequences of "the screen says quiz, the database says article":

**1. The stats lie in a specific, observable way.** When a question is added, `QuestionObserver` fires → `recalculateDuration` / `recalculatePoints` run on the lesson. Those methods branch on the lesson's **persisted** type. So a lesson you've toggled to quiz-and-added-three-questions-to still derives its duration and points by *article* rules (word count of an empty article = minimums). The left panel's stats show nonsense numbers until the next full save corrects them — drift, in a system we've spent this whole session making drift-proof.

**2. The article content's fate becomes ambiguous.** The article editor is a blur-commit inline editor. Toggle `article → quiz` while an unsaved paragraph sits in it, and the component unmounts — blur never fires, the paragraph vanishes. Under "the type is just a form value," that's a UI quirk. Under "every click persists," it's *data loss* with no warning.

**3. A lesson can exist in a state its own type forbids.** Type says quiz in your head, `article` in the row — meanwhile questions are being attached. The row's `article_content` isn't nulled (that only happens on metadata save), so you get an article-with-questions hybrid until Save sorts it out. The kind of half-state the outline architecture was supposed to make impossible.

## The two ways to finish making it live

**Option A — the type toggle persists instantly.** The type select becomes an inline editor like everything else: change it → a quiet PATCH writes `type` on the lesson row → `only: ['lesson']` partial reload → the database and the screen agree at all times. The metadata form slims down to title (+ exam duration, which I'd keep there since it's exam-specific and rarely touched). Consequences:

- The question outline is always building on a lesson whose type is *true* — the stats derivation is correct the moment you add question #1
- The `article_content` nulling happens at the toggle PATCH (type moves off article → content cleared, same hygiene the metadata save does today) — with one guard needed: the unmount-flush on the article editor (commit pending text *before* the swap) so nothing is silently lost
- One new edge to handle: toggling *to* `exam` triggers the "exam needs a duration" rule — the type PATCH can either carry the currently-entered duration or leave the lesson briefly duration-less until the form saves; I'd have the PATCH accept an optional duration and validate it when the target type is exam

**Option B — keep the form-based type, paper over the symptoms.** Patch the stats preview to *project* the selected type (compute what the numbers would be), maybe add a "type not saved yet" badge. Cheaper, but it's a second source of truth for the type — exactly the two-vocabularies problem you've been rejecting all session (column names vs. display names; observer vs. controller cascade; form-type vs. row-type would be the same disease).

## The shape of the difference

```
Option A (persist at toggle):
  toggle → PATCH type → DB is truth → panels render truth → stats true

Option B (form-local type):
  toggle → form is truth → panels render form → stats project a guess
                       → DB learns the truth later, maybe
```

Everything in this session's trajectory — outline persistence, observers, single source of truth — points at **A**. B is the last remaining "the screen knows something the database doesn't."

If A is the direction, the plan covers: type-select PATCH handler (+ exam-duration ripple), metadata form slimming to title/duration, `ArticleContent` unmount-flush, `LessonInformation` type field rewiring from form value to persisted value, and the small test updates. Say the word and I'll write it out fully — or tell me if you meant something narrower by "live."

what if i want to make the courses edit page fully live

## Assistant

The natural endpoint of everything we've built. Let me think through what "fully live" means for the course editor, because it's the same journey the lesson editor just completed — applied one level up, with a couple of new wrinkles.

## What's already live vs. what isn't

The course editor's **right panel (the outline) is already fully live**: modules and lessons CRUD + reorders all persist per-click, `only: ['course']` partial reloads, the works. That's the `CourseContent` architecture the lesson editor just inherited.

What's **not** live — the left panel, `CourseInformation`:

| Field | Current behavior |
|---|---|
| `status` (draft/published) | form value → saved by "Save Course" |
| `title`, `category`, `short_description`, `long_description` | form values → saved by "Save Course" |
| cover image | uploaded → **saved only by "Save Course"** (file rides the PUT) |
| `remove_image` flag | form state → applied by "Save Course" |
| stats (duration/modules/lessons/points) | server prop ✓ already truthful |

Plus the safety net around it all: the **zustand draft store** (`useCourseDraftStore`) exists *specifically* to preserve unsaved left-panel edits across the standalone lesson editor round-trip. If the left panel becomes live, that entire store becomes obsolete — there's nothing left to cache.

## The two wrinkles that make "course live" harder than "lesson live"

**1. Publishing is a transaction, not a field.** The lesson type toggle was one column. But `status: published` currently passes through `CourseUpdateRequest::after()` — the publish gatekeeper: *cover image must exist, at least one module must exist*. A naive "status is live now" toggle would let you publish a cover-less, module-less course, unless the gate moves into the status PATCH itself. So the status toggle gets the same treatment `updateType` gave the exam duration: **the rules travel with the write** — a PATCH to `status=published` that runs the publish checks and 422s (with the error flowing back to the toggle) when the course isn't ready. That's actually *better* UX than today: "Publish" fails fast with a clear reason instead of a failed form save at the end.

**2. The cover image is a file, and files ride forms.** Everything text (title, category, descriptions) can be a blur-commit inline editor — the `InlineTitleInput` contract, exactly like the article body just became. But `ImageUploader` holds a `File` object until some save event carries it. Options:
- **A. Image upload persists on selection** — the moment a file is picked, it uploads to its own endpoint (store new → delete obsolete after commit, the `QuestionController` audio pattern; `remove_image` becomes a plain DELETE-style PATCH). No form needed — files commit themselves.
- **B. Image stays on the Save button** — hybrid: text live, image manual. Ugly middle state; the cover would lag behind everything else.

A is the honest fully-live answer, and it has the exact shape we've already built twice (question audio, cover swap in `update`).

## The shape of the fully-live course editor

| Field | Persists via |
|---|---|
| title, category, descriptions | blur-commit inline PATCH (single-field endpoint, like `updateTitle`) |
| status (publish/unpublish) | instant toggle PATCH + publish gatekeeper on that endpoint |
| cover image | uploads on selection (new endpoint); removal on its own confirm action |
| modules/lessons | already live ✓ |
| stats | already observer/recalc-fed ✓ |

And the deletions this unlocks:
- **"Save Course" button disappears** — the entire `update` flow, the FormRequest's field rules, the multipart PUT, gone
- **`useCourseDraftStore` deleted** — nothing left to draft
- The editor page's react-hook-form → replaced by per-field local state (like `ArticleContent`)
- `CourseController::update` likely slims to nothing or near-nothing; `CourseUpdateRequest` dissolves into per-field requests (`title` reuses the rename pattern; the publish checks move to the status request's `after()`)

## The honest costs

1. **Bigger blast radius than the lesson work** — the course editor is the *root* of every scoped route; its page, its form, the draft store, the users of `existingImageUrl`/`removeImage` logic all change. Plus tests: the publish test, partial-metadata test, and image-replacement test all rewrite.
2. **The partial-list validation for status changes** — the draft/published toggle needs its own small endpoint + request, same ceremony as `updateType`.
3. **Publishing semantics worth pausing on** — should un-publishing (published → draft) also be a plain toggle? If a course has student enrollments someday, "draft" hides it — fine, but the endpoint should exist deliberately. Worth deciding now: full symmetry (toggle both ways) is what I'd build.
4. **`hasExistingImage` conditional validation on the frontend zod schema dissolves** — the publish gate becomes server-side-only on the status endpoint, which is cleaner anyway.

## The pattern you'd be completing

Notice what this gives you when it's done: **every editor in the app speaks one language** — course outline, lesson outline, question cards, answer rows, article body, metadata fields, toggles, uploads. No form anywhere, no Save button anywhere, no draft caches anywhere. The zustand store was the *last* piece of architecture that existed to compensate for a non-live panel; deleting it is the proof the design is finished.

Scope summary, if you green-light it: ~4 new endpoints (field PATCHes can share one or split; status; image), `CourseUpdateRequest` dissolved into focused requests, page + `CourseInformation` rewritten to inline-editors, draft store deleted, `CourseContent` untouched (already live), and the test suite rewritten for the new flow. It's the largest single change since the lesson redesign — but almost every piece is a pattern we've already built and tested twice.

## User

will zod even needed

---

## Assistant

Sharp question — and the honest answer is: **mostly no.** Zod's job shrinks to almost nothing in a fully-live editor, and it's worth seeing exactly why, because it's a beautiful illustration of what client-side validation is actually *for*.

## What zod does today — and why each duty disappears

Client-side form validation exists to answer one question: *"is this whole object valid enough to submit?"* — asked **before** sending, because submitting a form is expensive and the user would lose their work on rejection. Look at what the lesson editor's zod schemas currently check, and what happens to each duty when saves become per-field:

| Zod duty today | In a fully-live editor |
|---|---|
| `title: min(1)` before submit | The rename PATCH's server rule rejects empties; the **inline contract already skips empty locally** (the `InlineTitleInput` pattern: trim → empty/unchanged → *no request at all*). Client validation adds nothing the skip-guard doesn't already do |
| `type: enum` | The toggle sends one of three literal values from a select — can't be invalid locally |
| `duration: positive when exam` | The toggle PATCH carries the exam rule (`after()` on `LessonTypeUpdateRequest`) — server-side, as we just built |
| `article_content non-empty` | The blur-commit editor skips empty saves locally; server gate catches the rest |
| `answers 2–6, correct index in range` | The UI *structurally enforces* min-2 (delete hides at two) and max-6 (add disables at six); the radio can only point at rendered rows. Server rules remain the enforcement, UI is the convenience |
| `audio file required for listening` | The card save's server `after()` rule; the frontend shows the message through `onError` → `setError` |

**The pattern:** validation doesn't vanish — it *migrates back to the server, per write*. In a form world, the client pre-validates the whole object because a rejected submit is costly. In an outline world, every write is one field of one row, the server is the single rulebook, and the error comes back attached to exactly the field that failed — which react-hook-form's `setError` displays without zod having ever run.

## Where zod *does* survive — the small honest residue

Three places still earn their keep:

1. **Complex single-field formats** — if a field had real client-checkable structure (a slug regex, an email format, a max length you want to whisper about *before* the round-trip), zod refines on that one value still make sense as instant feedback. The course editor's fields (title, category, two descriptions) have no such structure — `max:255` on a title is the only candidate, and it's marginal.
2. **File validation before upload** — the `audioFileSchema` (size ≤ 10MB, MIME in mp3/wav/ogg) is genuinely useful client-side: rejecting a 50MB file *before* uploading it saves real time. This is the one zod piece I'd keep — and note it's not form validation at all, it's an **upload guard**. (Though even here you could hand-check two properties without zod.)
3. **Cross-field projection logic** — the draft-vs-publish conditional rules (`$requiredOrNullable`). Those dissolve completely once status is a server-gated toggle.

## And react-hook-form itself?

Worth asking, since it's the same question one layer down. Its remaining jobs in a live editor:
- **`setError`/`errors` display** for server rejections — still useful, but honestly replaceable by a `useState` error string per field (which `ArticleContent` already does! we built it with plain state, no RHF)
- `watch`/`setValue` plumbing — replaced by plain local state per inline editor

The lesson editor already demonstrates this split: the **metadata form** kept RHF+zod (still a mini-form), while `ArticleContent` and the answer rows went pure-state. If the course editor goes fully live, its left panel follows `ArticleContent` — local state, server errors, no resolver at all.

## The verdict, in one breath

> **Zod exists to pre-flight whole-form submissions. Fully-live editors don't submit whole forms — they send one field at a time and let the server's per-write rules answer. Validation doesn't disappear; it consolidates back into the Laravel FormRequests, which are already the single source of truth we've built all session. The survivors: an upload guard for files, and instant format feedback where a round-trip is genuinely expensive.**

So in the course plan: `createCourseSchema` and the metadata zod schemas get deleted alongside the form; `audioFileSchema` stays as an upload guard (or gets inlined into two property checks). The backend FormRequests — the ones we've been diligently building per endpoint — become the *only* validation layer, which is exactly where this whole session has been heading: one rulebook, one place, enforced on every write, no matter which client or path.

# How Lesson Content Works Today — The Full Picture

## One sentence

The lesson editor is a **server-driven outline**: the type toggle and every content mutation persist immediately through their own tiny endpoints, the article body is a blur-commit inline editor, and each question and answer is a row that only ever gets updated in place — never deleted-and-rebuilt.

## The page anatomy

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Lesson Editor page                                    │
│                                                       │
│ LEFT panel                RIGHT panel                 │
│ ───────────────           ───────────────────────     │
│ [metadata form]           [LessonContent]             │
│  · title        ──Save──►  keyed on lesson.type       │
│  · type select ──PATCH──►  (the SERVER type, which    │
│                             now always matches the    │
│  · exam time               screen — toggle persists)  │
│    limit        ──Save──►                              │
│  · stats preview           article → Wysiwyg editor   │
│                             quiz/exam → question cards │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Two independent things live on this page: a small form (title + exam limit) and a live outline. They share nothing — no giant form, no draft state, no zustand.

## The type toggle — instant

Changing the type select fires a quiet PATCH on the spot (`only: ['lesson']`, no progress bar). The server writes `type` + `duration` (exams must carry a positive limit — the rule travels with the toggle), the partial reload refreshes the page, and the right panel swaps variants **because the database changed** — not because a form value did. Article content and questions are *preserved* across toggles, so switching away and back loses nothing.

## The article variant — blur-commit

The Wysiwyg is an inline editor wearing a document's clothes:

- **Click outside → saves.** Unchanged or empty content sends nothing; a `committedRef` blocks double-fires
- **Discard link** reverts to server content
- **Status caption** narrates: *"152 words · Saved"* / *"Unsaved changes — click outside to save [Discard]"* / *"Saving…"*
- **Unmount flush** — if the type toggles away mid-typing, pending text commits before the panel swaps, so nothing is silently lost

## The quiz/exam variant — three nested outlines

**Level 1: the question list** (the `CourseContent` pattern, one level deeper)
- "Add Question" → POSTs a blank row (text type, empty content, next seat — *no* pre-seeded choices) → the list refreshes, card appears
- Drag → optimistic `arrayMove` + PATCH reorder (park-then-place on the backend, per the unique constraint)
- Delete → confirm dialog → DELETE (answers cascade, audio file cleaned after commit, siblings reindexed)

**Level 2: the question card** — each card is its own small react-hook-form
- Type select, Wysiwyg question text, audio upload, and the correct-answer radio live in card-local state
- **"Save Question"** → one multipart PATCH: fields + (if picked) the audio file + the radio index, which the server resolves to a `correct_answer_id`
- **Audio retention is free**: no new upload = the row keeps its file; a new upload = store new, delete old after commit
- Server rejections flow back into the card's error state (the `onError` → `setError` mapping)

**Level 3: the answers** — a server-driven micro-outline
- Each choice is a row with a stable ID; inline text edits save on Enter/blur (skip empty/unchanged — the rename contract)
- "Add Choice" POSTs immediately (max 6, enforced both sides); the delete button hides at 2 choices (min kept on the UI, backend restores the correct-answer pointer if the correct row dies)
- The **radio alone is card-state** — committed with "Save Question," because it writes the *question's* pointer, not the answer rows

## The write path — every endpoint owns one row

| Endpoint | Writes |
|---|---|
| `PUT lessons/{lesson}` | lesson row: title, type (re-affirmed), exam limit |
| `PATCH …/type` | lesson row: type + duration (instant toggle) |
| `PATCH …/content` | lesson row: article body |
| `POST/PATCH/DELETE questions/{question}` | question row: fields, audio, pointer, seats |
| `PATCH questions/reorder` | question rows: seats (parked then placed) |
| `POST/PATCH/DELETE answers/{answer}` | answer row: text, seats, pointer restore |

Every one validates through its own FormRequest, double-locked with its policy. No endpoint crosses a row boundary — that's the whole reason the old pain (delete-and-rebuild, audio ledgers, wildcard validation over three tables) is gone.

## How the numbers stay true

Two observers do the bookkeeping silently, for every write path:

- **`LessonObserver`** — `created`: +1 lesson counts on module and course; `updated`: re-derive points/duration, refresh module/course
- **`QuestionObserver`** — any question change: re-derive the lesson, refresh module and course

So the moment a question is added to a quiz, the duration/points preview in the left panel is already correct — derivation runs on the *persisted* type, which the instant toggle guarantees is truthful.

## The life of one lesson, end to end

1. Course outline → "Add Item" → blank lesson row (article, null duration) → editor opens
2. Toggle type to **quiz** → PATCH → panel swaps instantly, stats already quiz-derived
3. "+ Add Question" → POST → blank card appears with an empty choices list
4. Add two choices (each POSTs on click) → type the question text, mark a radio → **Save Question** → one PATCH; points become 10, duration derives
5. Drag the question up → optimistic swap + parked reorder
6. Add a third choice later, delete the correct one → pointer auto-restores
7. Toggle back to **article** to draft the reading → paragraph flushes on swap, quiz questions wait underneath untouched

Everything above is one consistent grammar: **properties on forms, structure as endpoints, and no save ever crossing a row boundary.**

Two parts — first the question, then the revision (which includes **two real bugs** I can diagnose from your report).

## Quiz → article: what happens to the 5 questions

**They're preserved, hidden, and waiting.** `updateType` doesn't delete anything — by the same data-preservation decision we made for article content: switching to article keeps all 5 question rows in the database, the derivation simply ignores them (article rules: words/150, words/10), and the article panel replaces the question outline. Toggle back to quiz later and all 5 questions reappear intact — audio, choices, correct answers, everything. The lesson carries both variants' data simultaneously; only `type` decides which one is *live*. (Optional nicety if you want it: a small "5 questions preserved" note on the article panel so nobody wonders where they went.)

## Your two bugs, diagnosed

**#4 "Add choice don't work" — found it, it's a route-parameter bug.** `AnswerChoicesInput` receives `routeParams` = `[course, module, lesson]` — but its routes need **four** params (`…lessons/{lesson}/questions/{question}/answers`). `route('…answers.store', routeParams)` builds a URL with a missing segment and dies silently. The rename/delete calls spread `[...routeParams, answerId]` — one short too. Fix: the card passes `[...routeParams, question.id]` into `AnswerChoicesInput`.

**#5 "Listening reverts to text" — explained by the card's architecture.** The question type only ever persisted through the **Save Question button** (the card was a mini-form). Toggle to listening, don't press Save, save the *lesson* form (which redirects away), come back — the row still says `text`. Your revision kills this bug structurally: no save button means every field must persist on its own trigger.

# Plan — The Question Card Goes Fully Live

## Backend: `QuestionController::update` becomes partial-write tolerant

One endpoint, partial payloads — each card interaction sends only its field:

| Trigger | PATCH payload |
|---|---|
| type select change | `{type}` |
| question text blur | `{question_content}` |
| radio change | `{correct_answer_index}` |
| audio picked (+ duration read) | multipart `{audio_file, audio_duration}` |
| audio removed | `{remove_audio: true}` |

**`QuestionUpdateRequest` rework:** every rule becomes `sometimes`; `after()` checks go conditional —
- bounds check (`index < answers count`) only when `correct_answer_index` is present
- the type switch to `text` clears audio in the controller (file deleted after commit); switching **to** `listening` is allowed freely — audio arrives when uploaded (the old "listening must have audio" was a save-time rule; there is no save anymore — it becomes a UI prompt, and the derivation already tolerates null audio)
- `remove_audio => sometimes|boolean` → nulls audio_url/duration, deletes file after commit

## Frontend: `QuestionCard` rewritten — form deleted

- **react-hook-form and `questionSchema` go away entirely** (the zod trajectory's conclusion) — pure local state per field, like `ArticleContent`
- **Type select** → immediate PATCH (optimistic; revert + error on failure) — the lesson-type-toggle pattern one level down; fixes bug #5
- **Question text** → the `ArticleContent` contract exactly: blur-commit, skip empty/unchanged, `committedRef`, Discard link, **unmount flush** (also fires on accordion collapse — collapsing *is* blurring), tiny status caption
- **Radio** → immediate PATCH on change (a discrete click, like any toggle)
- **Audio** → uploads on selection: blob preview shows instantly, Howler reads duration, the multipart PATCH fires once duration is known; Remove → `{remove_audio}`
- **No Save Question button** — deleted
- **`AnswerChoicesInput`** — receives `[...routeParams, question.id]` (bug #4 fix); choice rename/delete already work on their own triggers
- **Add Question** → already POSTs correctly; add the ID-diff auto-open so the new blank card appears expanded, ready to type (the `handleAddModule` trick from the course editor)

## Tests

- New regressions first: **listening toggle persists without any save button** (your bug #5 as a test), **add-choice route works** (bug #4)
- Partial-write coverage: each field PATCH alone; type→text clears audio after commit; `remove_audio`; radio bounds rejection
- Existing answer/reorder/scoped-ownership tests stay as-is

## Verification

Pint · `CoursesManagementTest` · ESLint on the card/choices/outline files · manual: toggle listening → navigate away → back → still listening; add choice → appears and persists; blur question text → saved.

190:                     >
191:                         Discard

193:                 )}
194:             </p>
195:         </>

202: function QuestionOutline({ routeParams, questions, sensors }) {

258:                 ...routeParams,

262:                 preserveScroll: true,
263:                 onStart: () => setIsDeleting(true),
264:                 onFinish: () => setIsDeleting(false),

270:     return (

280:             />
281: 
282:             {orderedQuestions.length === 0 ? (
283:                 <div className="rounded-2xl border border-dashed border-neutral-950/10 bg-neutral-50/50 p-8 text-center">
284:                     <p className="font-inter text-body-sm text-neutral-500">

286:                         to start building your exercise.
287:                     </p>

297:                             String(question.id),

325:                         : ''
326:                 }? This action cannot be undone.`}
327:                 confirmLabel="Delete Question"
328:                 onConfirm={handleConfirmDeleteQuestion}
329:                 isSubmitting={isDeleting}
330:             />
331:         </>
332:     );

335: /**
336:  * One persisted question — its own react-hook-form with zodResolver,
337:  * saving type, text, audio, and the correct-answer radio in one PATCH.
338:  */
339: function QuestionCard({ routeParams, question, index, onRequestDelete }) {
340:     const [isPending, setIsPending] = useState(false);
341: 
342:     const form = useForm({
343:         resolver: zodResolver(questionSchema),
344:         mode: 'onChange',
345:         defaultValues: {
346:             type: question.type,
347:             question_content: question.question_content,
348:             correct_answer_index: question.correct_answer_index,
349:             audio_file: null,
350:         },
351:     });
352: 
353:     const {
354:         watch,
355:         setValue,
356:         setError,
357:         clearErrors,
358:         handleSubmit,
359:         formState: { errors },
360:     } = form;
361:     const type = watch('type');
362:     const correctAnswerIndex = watch('correct_answer_index');
363: 
364:     // Local audio preview state — replaced by upload, null by remove.
365:     const [audio, setAudio] = useState({
366:         url: question.audio_url,
367:         filename: question.audio_filename,
368:         duration: question.audio_duration,
369:         file: null,
370:     });
371: 
372:     const onValid = (values) => {
373:         if (isPending) return;
374: 
375:         const formData = {
376:             type: values.type,
377:             question_content: values.question_content,
378:             correct_answer_index: values.correct_answer_index,
379:             _method: 'patch',
380:         };
381: 
382:         if (audio.file) {
383:             formData.audio_file = audio.file;
384:             formData.audio_duration = audio.duration;
385:         }
386: 
387:         router.post(
388:             route('dashboard.courses.modules.lessons.questions.update', [
389:                 ...routeParams,
390:                 question.id,
391:             ]),
392:             formData,
393:             {
394:                 forceFormData: true,
395:                 preserveScroll: true,
396:                 only: ['lesson'],
397:                 onStart: () => setIsPending(true),
398:                 onFinish: () => setIsPending(false),
399:                 onSuccess: () => setAudio((prev) => ({ ...prev, file: null })),
400:                 onError: (serverErrors) => {
401:                     clearErrors();
402:                     for (const [path, message] of Object.entries(
403:                         serverErrors ?? {},
404:                     )) {
405:                         setError(path, { type: 'server', message });
406:                     }
407:                 },
408:             },
409:         );
410:     };
411: 
412:     return (
413:         <FormProvider {...form}>
414:             <CollapsibleSection
415:                 value={String(question.id)}
416:                 dragId={String(question.id)}
417:                 header={
418:                     <span className="font-poppins text-body-sm font-bold text-neutral-950">
419:                         Question {index + 1}
420:                     </span>
421:                 }
422:                 actions={
423:                     <button
424:                         type="button"
425:                         onClick={onRequestDelete}
426:                         className="hover:bg-error-50 hover:text-error-500 cursor-pointer rounded-lg p-1 text-neutral-500 transition-colors"
427:                         title="Delete Question"
428:                     >
429:                         <Trash2 className="size-3.5" />
430:                     </button>
431:                 }
432:             >
433:                 <form
434:                     onSubmit={handleSubmit(onValid)}
435:                     className="flex flex-col gap-4"
436:                 >
437:                     <SelectField
438:                         name="type"
439:                         label="Question Type"
440:                         options={QUESTION_TYPES}
441:                         value={type}
442:                         onValueChange={(val) =>
443:                             setValue('type', val, {
444:                                 shouldValidate: true,
445:                                 shouldDirty: true,
446:                             })
447:                         }
448:                         errorMessage={errors.type?.message}
449:                     />
450: 
451:                     {type === 'listening' && (
452:                         <AudioUploadInput
453:                             audioUrl={audio.url}
454:                             audioFilename={audio.filename}
455:                             audioDuration={audio.duration}
456:                             onUpload={(file) => {
457:                                 const objectUrl = URL.createObjectURL(file);
458:                                 if (audio.url?.startsWith('blob:')) {
459:                                     URL.revokeObjectURL(audio.url);
460:                                 }
461:                                 setAudio({
462:                                     url: objectUrl,
463:                                     filename: file.name,
464:                                     duration: null,
465:                                     file,
466:                                 });
467:                             }}
468:                             onRemove={() => {
469:                                 if (audio.url?.startsWith('blob:')) {
470:                                     URL.revokeObjectURL(audio.url);
471:                                 }
472:                                 setAudio({
473:                                     url: null,
474:                                     filename: null,
475:                                     duration: null,
476:                                     file: null,
477:                                 });
478:                             }}
479:                             onDurationRead={(duration) =>
480:                                 setAudio((prev) => ({
481:                                     ...prev,
482:                                     duration: Math.round(duration),
483:                                 }))
484:                             }
485:                             errorMessage={errors.audio_file?.message}
486:                         />
487:                     )}
488: 
489:                     <div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
490:                         <label className="font-inter text-body-sm block font-bold text-neutral-700">
491:                             Question Text{' '}
492:                             <span className="text-error-500">*</span>
493:                         </label>
494:                         <WysiwygEditor
495:                             value={watch('question_content')}
496:                             onChange={(html) =>
497:                                 setValue('question_content', html, {
498:                                     shouldValidate: true,
499:                                     shouldDirty: true,
500:                                 })
501:                             }
502:                             placeholder="Enter your question here..."
503:                             variant="compact"
504:                         />
505:                         {errors.question_content?.message && (
506:                             <p className="font-inter text-caption text-error-500">
507:                                 {errors.question_content.message}
508:                             </p>
509:                         )}
510:                     </div>
511: 
512:                     <AnswerChoicesInput

515:                         correctChoiceIndex={correctAnswerIndex}
516:                         onCorrectChoiceIndexChange={(idx) =>

518:                                 shouldValidate: true,
519:                                 shouldDirty: true,
520:                             })
521:                         }
522:                         isSubmitting={isPending}
523:                         errorMessage={
524:                             errors.correct_answer_index?.message ?? ''
525:                         }
526:                     />
527: 
528:                     <div className="flex justify-end">
529:                         <Button type="submit" loading={isPending}>
530:                             Save Question
531:                         </Button>
532:                     </div>
533:                 </form>
534:             </CollapsibleSection>
535:         </FormProvider>
536:     );
537: }

24: /**
25:  * Shared inline title input used by both module headers and lesson bars.
26:  * Guards against double submission on Enter + onBlur and ignores empty or
27:  * unchanged names.
28:  */
29: function InlineTitleInput({ initialTitle, onSave, onCancel, className }) {
30:     const [text, setText] = useState(initialTitle);
31:     const committedRef = useRef(false);
32: 
33:     const commit = () => {
34:         if (committedRef.current) {
35:             return;
36:         }
37:         committedRef.current = true;
38: 
39:         const trimmed = text.trim();
40:         if (!trimmed || trimmed === initialTitle) {
41:             onCancel();
42:             return;
43:         }
44: 
45:         onSave(trimmed);
46:         onCancel();
47:     };
48: 
49:     return (
50:         <input
51:             type="text"
52:             value={text}
53:             onChange={(e) => setText(e.target.value)}
54:             onBlur={commit}
55:             onKeyDown={(e) => {
56:                 if (e.key === 'Enter') {
57:                     e.preventDefault();
58:                     commit();
59:                 } else if (e.key === 'Escape') {
60:                     e.preventDefault();
61:                     committedRef.current = true;
62:                     onCancel();
63:                 }
64:             }}
65:             onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
66:             className={className}
67:             autoFocus
68:         />
69:     );
70: }

109:     };

19: export function createCourseSchema(hasExistingImage = false, categories = []) {

23:             title: z.string().trim().max(255),
24:             category: z

26:                 .refine(

31:             long_description: z.string().trim(),
32:             image: courseImageRule.nullable(),
33:         })
34:         .superRefine((data, ctx) => {
35:             if (data.status !== 'published') {
36:                 return;
37:             }
38:

40:                 ctx.addIssue({
41:                     code: 'custom',

43:                     message: 'Course title is required',
44:                 });
45:             }
46:

54:

151: /**
152:  * Inline choice editor — commits on Enter/blur, skips empty/unchanged
153:  * values (the same contract as the outline's InlineTitleInput).
154:  */
155: function ChoiceText({ answerId, initialContent, onSubmit, placeholder }) {
156:     const [text, setText] = useState(initialContent);
157:     const [committed, setCommitted] = useState(false);
158: 
159:     const commit = () => {
160:         if (committed) return;
161: 
162:         const trimmed = text.trim();
163: 
164:         if (!trimmed || trimmed === initialContent) {
165:             setText(initialContent);
166:             return;
167:         }
168: 
169:         setCommitted(true);
170:         onSubmit(answerId, trimmed, () => {
171:             setCommitted(false);
172:         });
173:     };
174: 
175:     return (
176:         <input
177:             type="text"
178:             value={text}
179:             onChange={(e) => setText(e.target.value)}
180:             onBlur={commit}
181:             onKeyDown={(e) => {
182:                 if (e.key === 'Enter') {
183:                     e.preventDefault();
184:                     commit();
185:                 } else if (e.key === 'Escape') {
186:                     e.preventDefault();
187:                     setText(initialContent);
188:                     setCommitted(true);
189:                 }
190:             }}
191:             placeholder={placeholder}
192:             className="font-inter text-body-sm flex-grow border-none bg-transparent px-1 text-neutral-950 outline-none"
193:         />
194:     );
195: }

 * Controlled answer-choices list editor. Renders the choice rows,

    choices = [],
    correctChoiceIndex,
    onCorrectChoiceIndexChange,
    onAddChoice,
    onRenameChoice,
    onDeleteChoice,
    maxChoices = MAX_CHOICES,
    minChoices = MIN_CHOICES,
    errorMessage = '',
    className = '',
}) {
    return (
        <div
            className={`space-y-2 border-t border-neutral-950/5 pt-2 ${className}`}
        >
            <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
                <label className="font-inter text-body-sm font-bold text-neutral-700">
                    Answer Choices <span className="text-error-500">*</span>
                </label>
                <button
                    type="button"
                    disabled={choices.length >= maxChoices}
                    onClick={() => onAddChoice?.()}
                    className="..."
                >
                    <Plus className="size-3" />
                    <span>Add Choice</span>
                </button>
            </div>

            <div className="space-y-2.5">
                {choices.map((choice, choiceIdx) => (
                    <div key={choice.id} className="...">
                        <input
                            type="radio"
                            name={`correct-choice-${choice.question_id ?? 'new'}-${choice.id}`}
                            ...
                        />
                        <ChoiceText
                            answerId={choice.id}
                            initialContent={choice.answer_content}
                            onSubmit={onRenameChoice}
                            placeholder={`Choice ${choiceIdx + 1}`}
                        />
                        {choices.length > minChoices && (
                            <button onClick={() => onDeleteChoice?.(choice.id)} ...>
                                <X />
                            </button>
                        )}
                    </div>
                ))}
            </div>

            {errorMessage && <p ...>{errorMessage}</p>}
        </div>
    );
}

}
